# The Depths He Measures with His Hand

## Scripture
*"Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or with the breadth of his hand marked off the heavens?"* — Isaiah 40:12

## Reflection
Step outside on a clear September night and look up. If you live far from city lights, you may glimpse the Milky Way—a faint, milky band arching overhead. What you're seeing is our galaxy edge-on: billions of stars, clouds of gas, and dust so vast that light needs a hundred thousand years to cross it. And our galaxy is only one of hundreds of billions.

Now consider this: Isaiah says God marks off the heavens with the breadth of His hand.

The same hand that flung galaxies into place cradles the oceans. The same palm that spans unimaginable distances also holds your restless heart. This is the God who is not overwhelmed by the scale of His own creation—and therefore is never overwhelmed by the scale of your need.

Sometimes our problems feel galaxy-sized. We wonder if anyone truly sees the whole of it. But the One who measures the heavens with a handspan has already numbered the hairs of your head. Distance does not diminish His attention. Vastness does not exhaust His care.

Tonight, let the size of the sky not shrink you—let it enlarge your view of Him. The God who holds the cosmos holds you.

## Prayer
Lord, when my worries feel as vast as the heavens, remind me that You measure them all with Your hand. Thank You that the God of galaxies is also the God who draws near. Hold me tonight, and let Your greatness bring me peace. Amen.
